rationale: TruLens is suitable for the scoped offline retrieval-ID pilot using the tested forbidden provider and explicit input validation. Both frameworks matched on valid synthetic fixtures and made zero observed network attempts, so winner not established on the highest-priority criterion. TruLens offers practical pilot advantages: its tested methods emitted no deprecation warning, while the Ragas metrics have an explicit removal warning, and its isolated trial environment contained fewer distributions. These findings do not establish retrieval-quality or semantic-evaluation superiority.
separating_test: Run both adapters on the same frozen six-query CRA2 corpus set; require identical ID-score semantics, no egress, and correct empty/malformed-score failures. If tied, no retrieval-quality winner is established.
